A monsoon surge continues just south of the Marianas as Typhoon
Dolphin, centered near 23N152E, treks west-northwestward away from 
Minamitorishima. Scatterometry this morning shows an extensive area 
of 20 to 30 knot west to southwest winds to the south of Guam,
stretching eastward to the north of Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae,
accompanying a band of numerous showers and isolated to scattered
thunderstorms. These fresh to strong westerlies and associated
convection will gradually build northwest into the area over the next
few days as Dolphin passes north of the area near Iwo To. Windy
conditions are expected to develop for Guam on Monday and increase
Tuesday as the monsoon surge expands northward across the CNMI, with
models indicating a peak in winds and showers around Tuesday and 
Tuesday night. Winds will relax slightly Wednesday through Friday,
becoming moderate to fresh as Dolphin pulls away and a col area 
develops near or east of the far northern CNMI. Then, the monsoon
trough and surge look to shift back toward the south and 
reinvigorate across the area this coming weekend.

The increase in winds, wind waves, and building swells from Typhoon 
Dolphin and its associated monsoon pattern, will bring marine and 
surf hazards across the region for much of the week, discussed in the
section below. Currently, a Small Craft Advisory remains in effect 
for Guam, and will also go into effect for Rota, Tinian, and Saipan 
at 6 AM ChST Monday morning. A High Risk of Rip Currents remains in 
effect along east facing reefs, but will extend to north facing reefs
at 10 PM ChST tonight. At that time, a High Surf Advisory goes into 
effect for north and east facing reefs.

Marine/Surf...
Fresh to strong westerlies will continue across Guam coastal 
waters, generating choppy seas hazardous to small craft, which 
will spread northward across the CNMI over the next day or two. 
Winds will peak in the first half of this week, with a possibility
of frequent gale-force gusts Monday and Tuesday, which would 
necessitate a Gale Warning at that time. Additionally, distant 
Typhoon Dolphin (12W) is generating a long-period east to northeast 
swell that is moving through the Marianas, which will gradually shift
north over the next day or so, then shift to the northwest. 
Meanwhile, the developing monsoon pattern will lead to increasing 
southwesterly swell over the coming days. These increasing swells and
wind waves will build combined seas to exceed 10 feet across the 
coastal waters, maintaining hazardous sea conditions for much of this
week.

The long-period east to northeast swell will maintain a high risk of
rip currents along east facing reefs of the Marianas, spreading to 
north-facing reefs beginning tonight, with hazardous surf also 
expected to develop along north and east-facing reefs tonight. For
now, the risk of rip currents remains moderate for south and west
facing reefs. As Dolphin passes the far northern CNMI, the long- 
period swell direction is expected to shift north over the next few 
days, and then northwest around midweek. As it does so, a high risk 
of rip currents, and hazardous surf, is expected to develop along 
west facing reefs later this week. A moderate risk of lightning is 
expected through at least Tuesday.

Tropical Systems...
Typhoon Dolphin continues to move west-northwest over the far
northern portion of the Guam Area of Responsibility (AOR). Dolphin 
is expected to continue west to west-northwest over the next few 
days, moving away from Minamitorishima and approaching Iwo To. 
Latest guidance shows Dolphin slowly weakening as it moves farther 
away. 

For more information on Dolphin, please refer to bulletins issued by 
the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 PGTW and by
the National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
A dry pattern is now setting up over eastern Micronesia as Typhoon
Dolphin continues to pull the monsoon trough farther north. Only
partly cloudy skies with isolated showers are expected at Pohnpei and
Kosrae through the end of the week. For Majuro, lingering convection
will result in scattered showers and possibly a thunderstorms or two
through Monday afternoon, with drier conditions as the eastern end
of the monsoon trough pulls farther north.

For the marine forecast, winds and seas are expected to remain below
hazardous levels for small craft operations, however, due to the mix
of wind waves, north and west swell at Pohnpei and Kosrae, seas will
still be choppy. Combined seas will continue to slowly subside over
the next few days. Moderate to fresh winds at Pohnpei will diminish 
overnight, but remain gentle to moderate through the end of the week.
For Kosrae and Majuro, light to gentle winds are expected through 
the week.
